structured_output.text: Proved only L(N) <= (1+o(1)) log N: for a k-term prime AP (k>=3, beyond small degenerate cases), every prime p<k divides d, so d >= prod_{p<k} p = e^{(1+o(1))k}, and (k-1)d < N. The claim L(N)=o(log N) is conjecturally true (Hardy-Littlewood heuristics suggest L(N) ~ log N / log log N order), but I have no proof; it appears open. Answer: believed yes, not proven.
